title: Joining and views of the musicians' union
summary: Joined in 1946; strict union under Petrillo, fines, right-to-work, non-union bands on Bourbon Street.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger

blocks.x: When did you join the Musician Union? When was that? I joined the Musician Union in 1946. Okay. When did you join the Musician Union?
I joined the Musician Union in 1946.
Wallace Davenport reel number four November 14 1995 Yeah, you joined the union, did you have to join the union? Yeah.

If you're going to play a union job. Because if you didn't belong to a union, or belong to the union, the musicians with the jobs who were union musicians, they wouldn't hire you. And if you join the union and you play with musicians who are not in the union, they put a fine on you, they put you out.

Petrillo when he was president of the whole union board all over America, they were very strict. And like a musician who was not a union musician and he was playing a job. See Petrillo is a group of gangsters. They come up and break your arm or break your horn up. And you couldn't do anything about it.
So did you adhere to the union rules and regulations? Oh yeah.

Because once they put a fine on you, they put a fine on you, put you out of the union, you're in trouble. Right. You can't get a job unless you work with a non-union. But now like on Bourbon Street now, I think my band is about the only union band on Bourbon Street.

Yeah, but you can't, but now like if I would play with a non-union band, they would put me at the union, they would fine me. Put a fine on me.

But they couldn't stop the non-union band from working there. As long as, now like they would have two bands, a non-union band and a union band. At one time they wouldn't let that go, but they'd let it go now. Because the guy said, well look, I want this non-union band to play in my plays. Now the famous Doe, they have two bands, but I think both of the bands are non-union. I think I'm the only one on Bourbon Street with a union band. But see now, those guys who work with the non-union band, they'll play, they get so much a set. So much a set. Now if they come to work and it starts raining and they play one set, the guy tell them you can go home, pay them for one set. But they can't do that with a union contract.

So you haven't had a real, I've heard a lot of people have had real run-ins with the union off and on over the years. I've heard guys in the union complain about the union. Oh yeah. That they don't do much for the musician, they don't. Well they don't do anything for the musicians.
They don't get jobs for the musicians. The only thing when you get a job is if you do something wrong. Like if you don't show up on time, they put a fine on you.
